title: Agenda: Matthew and Cyrus, Friday 2026-11-27, 09:00 Mountain
sub: The topics Matthew brings to his meeting with Cyrus on Friday 2026-11-27 at about 09:00 Mountain time (MST). The last agenda was for their meeting of Friday 2026-11-13 (^report(42)). Since then the team met on 11-17 (^report(54)), Cyrus confirmed SInt's 64 bits on 11-18, and the team held a merge-a-thon on 11-19 (^report(58)). “Last week” below is the state as of Friday 2026-11-20, just after those; “this week” is now, after the night of 11-26. A work in progress: each item says where it stands, as of when, and what it needs from the meeting.
short: After the meeting: hazel-jit and the npm package look good, maybe a couple of weeks from dev; next week, a jit subcommand for Hazel's CLI and a tree of Livelit applications slides (Notes from the meeting).
The two PRs: hazel-jit (#2859) and the package (#2857) both build on dev now; the games run at 3.8× plain JS, from 11.9×; five green trials wait.
The back burner: 46 open PRs, 24 drafts; three merged at the merge-a-thon; SInt's 64 bits (#2828), the README (#2812) and the font and icons wait.
If there is time: Cyrus's advice on an email from Max Carroll, which Matthew brings; and a demo of Gnome dig and Gnome world 0.0.146, with N's flying jellyfish.

sections.title: 1. The two PRs: hazel-jit and the hazeljs package
sections.intro: Matthew's focus, agreed with Cyrus: the npm package and hazel-jit (his words, 11-25). By his rule of 11-23, hazel-jit lives in at most two PRs, both for dev: its own, #2859, and the package's, #2857, which merges it. Each item compares last week (11-20) with now.

items.title: hazel-jit: last week against this week
items.status: one PR from dev since 11-23 (#2859, CI green); the games now 3.8× plain JS's time, from 11.9× on 11-19; a division trial green, waiting on Matthew's word
items.as_of: 2026-11-27 07:05 MST (git, gh, npm and the dashboard read then)
items.body:
Last week, as of Friday 11-20: hazel-jit lived on the livelits line's trial branches, none of them from dev: #2817 (trial/694-view-jit: livelit views and a slide's whole run), trial/794-games-aot (the games compiled ahead of time) and trial/758-sint64-jit. The npm package did not have it (hazeljs 0.0.8 ran the interpreter only). On the games of hazeljs-examples it took 11.9 times the time of each game's plain JS (^report(65)).

This week:

  • One home, from dev (11-23). #2859, branch hazel-jit, a draft from dev at 21da4ae66b, after dev's move to Jane Street Core: the compiler, the values across, and mixed mode, where the interpreter calls a program's fully typed functions compiled. 25 commits, 5,704 lines added and 4 removed; CI green. Of the 289 evaluator checks, 234 compile and 211 of those give the interpreter's answer, none differs (the other 23 end in something that is not a value; CI run 45540053889). Nothing in the app turns it on yet. By Matthew's rule of 11-23, the jit lives in this PR and in the package's, #2857, which merges it.
  • Its output now reads like ReScript's and Melange's (11-24, 11-25): records as plain JS objects, a named function's tuple parts as JS arguments, a function's tail calls of itself as loops, constructors without arguments made once, a module's members by name, === against a literal (^ticket(847), ^ticket(853)). On the 14 games: 3.8 times plain JS, from 11.9 on 11-19, and 4,148 times as fast as the interpreter (GitHub run 45666570615, every answer the same four ways; the figure).
  • Holes (merged 11-26 on Matthew's word): in mixed mode an argument's hole crosses into compiled code unopened, and code with holes compiles; only a call that looks inside a hole falls back (^ticket(769)). John (johnya) is on probes now, so holes are ours.
  • The night of 11-26: trial/891-idiv (off hazel-jit, 664c49c49a, CI green): Int division as Math.trunc(a / b) + 0, and Int arithmetic on numbers written out folded at compile time. Gnome world's World.step about 40% faster on fresh inputs (5.15–5.25 µs to 3.02–3.19, one GitHub runner, three rounds), and a −0 the interpreter never gives is gone (^ticket(891)). With the four package trials (item 2), all five merged on trial/1126-night (abf653a21d, CI green, run 45943307054, 5,227 tests): World.step about 39% faster than the hazeljs branch (3.78–4.06 µs to 2.33–2.48; the figure).
  • The livelits line: #2817 has a one-line fix to LivelitProj's view memo (1a8afab5ae, CI green, ^ticket(887)): the Witch's neck drag with compiling off now draws its view in 6.4 ms a frame (about 156 fps), compiled 5.0 ms (about 200 fps), one run in Firefox.
items.decided: Looks good; maybe a couple of weeks from merging to dev.
items.meeting: Merge trial/891-idiv into hazel-jit (#2859), and so into hazeljs (#2857)? What does #2859 need before it leaves draft for dev: which reviewer, and is the agreement sweep (211 agree, none differs) the right gate? SInt is 64 bits (settled 11-19), but dev still wraps a 32-bit SInt, so #2859 holds its SInt tests back until #2828 lands (item 3).

items.title: hazeljs, the npm package: last week against this week
items.status: 0.0.14 on npm since 11-25, the first with hazel-jit; #2857 CI green; four trials green, waiting on Matthew's word
items.as_of: 2026-11-27 07:05 MST (git, gh, npm and the dashboard read then)
items.body:
Last week, as of Friday 11-20: npm's latest was 0.0.8 (11-17): hazel-lib.js built from #2719's branch, the interpreter only, and hazel-listings.js. On 11-19 Cyrus asked the team to review the package's API and packaging (^ticket(773)); that day the editor moved into the package, loading nothing from elsewhere (0.0.9, not published), with a font and icons of its own (#2837, #2842).

This week:

  • One branch for the package (11-23): #2857, branch hazeljs, a draft against dev, holds what the package is built from: the library (#2711, #2719), the editable embed (#2814), the font and icons, dev on Core, and hazel-jit by merging #2859, never by copying. 91 commits, 13,049 lines added; CI green. Hazel.jit and Hazel.compile are in the library.
  • The JS boundary: values converted by the declared type, straight into compiled code's shapes; what was converted remembered by links on the objects (Mahjong solitaire's run 2.5 times as fast, ca851b422d). ^report(64) was corrected: on fresh inputs, as a game gives them, the pieces that take lists cost 7 to 9 times their JS, not 2 to 4; the earlier timings reused the same objects, which the converters remember.
  • npm: 0.0.14 (11-25), published from Matthew's sign-in, the first since 0.0.8: hazel-jit's loops, JS arguments, constructors made once. 0.0.9 to 0.0.13 were made in the repository but not published (the figure).
  • The night of 11-26, four trials off hazeljs, each CI green on its own:
    • ^ticket(890) trial/890-saved-program: Hazel.jitProgramSaved lets a page keep its compiled rules. Gnome world, with this trial library, has its rules ready 0.68 to 0.70 s after a reload, against 13.6 to 14.4 s for a cold build (one browser).
    • ^ticket(681) trial/681-memo-big: the converters stop remembering small conversions. On fresh copies, Solitaire 30 to 8.6 ms and Mahjong solitaire 33 to 12; on the same objects again most within 5%, a few slower (Solitaire 3.32 to 3.79 ms), and Minesweeper slower on fresh copies (13 to 16 ms).
    • ^ticket(792) trial/792-big-ints: an Int past 2^31 from JS arrives whole (a safe whole number to 2^53, a BigInt past it).
    • ^ticket(791) trial/791-labels-linear: two quadratic labeled-tuple helpers in Hazel's statics made linear; a build about 9% faster (warm 4.10–4.20 s to 3.77–3.79). LabeledTuple.re is shared Hazel code.
  • Why a build takes seconds when the jit is fast (Matthew's question, 11-27): the jit makes the rules run fast (Gnome world's step takes microseconds); building them is a one-time cost, and nearly all of it comes before hazel-jit compiles anything, as Hazel parses the rules and type-checks them. A CPU profile of Gnome world's build (^report(64)) puts 70% of it in the statics (Statics.re, inclusive), 31% in operations on types (Typ.meet, the common type of two branches, and matching labeled tuples' fields by name), 16% in LabeledTuple.re, 14% in the map of each term's information, and 28% in garbage collection (the parts overlap: each counts what it calls); the parser does not show, and hazel-jit's compiling is 0.5%, about 0.1 s. The statics are the editor's, built for live feedback: they record every term's type and context for the cursor's inspector, which a compile does not need. And Gnome world's rules are heavy in records (the gnome has 17 named fields), each field matched by name in every function; the birds' module, with the most and largest records, costs about three times the world's per character. In Node on a GitHub runner a build is about 5 s; in a browser on Matthew's laptop, 13.6 to 16.5 s this week. Together the trials make it about 8% faster (the figure); kept rules (890) skip it on a reload.
  • An experiment this morning, for numbers only, not to merge (^ticket(894)): every let analyzes its definition twice on the hazeljs branch (a probe for recursion, then the real pass), and three times when it might be recursive, so lets nested in definitions multiply, 2 to the depth; and a module binding analyzes its whole definition twice more. Two open PRs address this: #2603 (a let analyzed once unless it refers to itself; meet asked once per node, not three times) and #2717 (a module binding analyzes its definition once). Their three commits were ported to Core by hand onto the night's trials, as trial/1127-statics (ba32db7481; #2603's context index left out, as it conflicts). Gnome world's rules built in Node, all three libraries on one GitHub runner, three rounds (build timing run 46023240545): warm, 0.33 to 0.34 s against 2.87 to 3.19 s for the night's trials and 3.14 to 3.32 s for hazeljs, about 9 times as fast; the first build of a process 1.39 to 1.58 s against 3.94 to 4.44 and 4.34 to 5.09. Every piece of Gnome world gives the same answers as its JavaScript twin with the trial library, as with the night's (fresh timing run 46023247014: the gnome, the carpet, the cat tail, Clover, the boulders, picking up, the wind, the bunnies, frogs and birds). Hazel's own test suite on the trial was still running when this was written.
items.decided: Looks good too; maybe a couple of weeks from merging to dev, as hazel-jit.
items.meeting: Take the four trials into hazeljs (#2857) and publish 0.0.15? jitProgramSaved is an addition to the package's API. Should 791 go to dev as a small PR of its own, since LabeledTuple is shared code? And who on the team reviews the package's API and packaging, as Cyrus asked on 11-19? Since a build is nearly all the statics: is a build-only mode of the statics (no per-term information for the editor) worth doing, given they are shared code? And #2603 and #2717, which make Gnome world's build about 9 times as fast: who reviews them, and do they go to dev before the package?

next: On Matthew's word: trial/891-idiv into hazel-jit (#2859); the four package trials into hazeljs (#2857); then hazeljs 0.0.15.
791's two commits as a small PR to dev, if agreed.
#2859 out of draft, with the reviewer the meeting names.

items.title: The back burner: the other open PRs
items.status: 46 open, 24 of them drafts; 3 merged at the 11-19 merge-a-thon; a few to settle
items.as_of: 2026-11-27 07:05 MST (git, gh, npm and the dashboard read then)
items.body:
Since the last agenda: at the merge-a-thon of 11-19 (^report(58), which found 14 of 48 ready for only an approval) three merged: #2613 (every color a stylesheet reads, the theme defines), #2652 (the eval worker starts at load) and #2816 (ids as strings, evaluation about 13% faster on the heaviest programs); #2490, the wasm_of_ocaml spike, was closed. That evening dev moved to Jane Street Core (#2470 and the PRs stacked on it), after most of these PRs were written.

Worth a word today:

  • #2828, SInt has 64 bits everywhere, and overflow is an error (draft, CI green, no review yet, last changed 11-19). The width is settled (Cyrus 11-18, Matthew 11-19: 64 bits). Until it lands, dev wraps a 32-bit SInt where hazel-jit stops at an overflow, so #2859 holds those tests back.
  • #2812, Hazel's README links to hazeljs (from ^report(42); a draft, review asked of Cyrus and the hazel-core team, none yet; CI green). The package has changed since: 0.0.14, with hazel-jit.
  • #2837, IBM Plex Sans in place of Helvetica Neue, and #2842, Material Icons shipped (11-19, ready, against dev): the team's font question of 11-19. Both are already inside #2857.
  • The JS library's stack, #2711, #2719 and #2814: #2857 is built from them. Keep them open, or close them in favor of #2857?
  • The livelits line, #2597, #2635, #2817 and #2819: kept for now (Matthew, 11-23), no longer the only critical path (11-25).
  • The performance PRs to dev (#2603, #2606, #2661, #2671, #2673, #2675, #2681 and others, 09-26 to 10-13): written before dev's move to Core; whether each still merges cleanly is not checked here.
items.meeting: Which of these should move this week: #2828 (so #2859's SInt tests return), #2812, or #2837 and #2842? Close the JS library's stack in favor of #2857? And the older performance PRs: rebase them onto Core, or park them?

items.title: A demo: Gnome dig and Gnome world
items.asked: Matthew (his list, item 5, if there is time)
items.status: Gnome world 0.0.148 live 11-27 08:28: its rules compiled ahead of time (ready in 188 ms, no build), the flying level, the flying jellyfish
items.body:
Two games in hazeljs-examples whose rules are written in Hazel and run in the page through hazeljs and hazel-jit, each with a twin in plain JS for checks: Gnome dig and Gnome world. Cyrus endorsed such game workloads as a corpus of Hazel code that is organically demanded (Matthew, 11-25).

Last week, as of 11-20, the repository was at 0.0.40, before either game: its VERSIONS.md first names Gnome dig at 0.0.61 (11-22) and Gnome world at 0.0.76 (11-23).

This week: Gnome world's rules are eleven Hazel modules (the figure), from World.hz on 11-23 to the animals on 11-26 and the jellyfish on 11-27. In 0.0.141 to 0.0.143 the bunnies', frogs' and birds' minds became Hazel, each checked against its JS twin on 600,000 of 600,000 steps in Node. N's level, 🌈 The rainbow sky, is 0.0.140. In 0.0.144 and 0.0.145 a page keeps its built rules between loads, but only with the trial library (?libat=trial/890-saved-program); with the shipped library each load still builds them (item 2). Its speed run of 44,933 steps takes 25.5 s with hazel-jit against 24.7 s in plain JS; the interpreter took 227.6 s for 42,000 of them (^report(65)). With the five trials of 11-26 (trial/1126-night) a whole step in the page takes 1.92–2.05 ms with Hazel against 1.77–1.86 plain, well inside a 60 fps frame of 16.7 ms.

New this morning, 0.0.147 and 0.0.148 (live 08:28; the world save check green, both levels as recorded): the rules compiled ahead of time, at Matthew's ask: a GitHub job compiles Gnome world's rules once with the night's trial library (Hazel.jitProgramSaved, ^ticket(890)) and commits the program as text; the live page made its rules from it in 188 ms, with no build, against 4 to 16 s, and kept them when the library loaded after. And the flying level, as N wants it (^ticket(895)): its land 40 rows lower (more sky, half the ground), gnome house pods down ladders with power ups, 253 turning coins in the sky, the rainbow clouds within sight (they were all out of sight, 12 to 40 rows up), the portals labelled, and a welcome that says what to do.

New this morning, 0.0.146 (commit 2026142, pushed 07:07, live 07:09; its world save check is green, GitHub run 46013126230, and it ran Jelly.step against its JS twin again there: the same at 40,000 of 40,000 steps): the flying jellyfish, N's ask. Hold ↑ and press J: it hovers, each ↑ is a pulse that shoots it up like a rocket, and it bursts rainbow clouds for points and glows in their colours. Its flight is Hazel's new module, Jelly.step, with a JS twin; the Node check, run on the laptop with the hazeljs library of 11-25, gives the same answer at 40,000 of 40,000 steps, 1.7 µs a step through the jit against 0.45 µs in JS. With it, the rules compiled in the page in 16.5 s.
items.meeting: A five-minute look at both games on Matthew's screen. What would Cyrus want measured, or written up, from this corpus?

method: Started 2026-11-27 from Matthew's list for the meeting, in his order. Public from its first draft, as agendas are, and republished as items move. Sentence highlights (Matthew, 11-27): click any sentence to mark it pre discussion; again, post discussion; again, not highlighted; kept in your browser, and listed at the end in order.
Every number names its source: a ticket on the work dashboard, a report in this series, a GitHub run, a commit, or npm view. PRs are hazelgrove/hazel's unless named otherwise.
Each item has a copy item chip: it copies the item's number, its id (which stays when items are reordered), its title and its link.
decided: hazel-jit looks good: maybe a couple of weeks from merging to dev (#2859).
Ditto for the npm package work (hazeljs, #2857): maybe a couple of weeks from dev.
Next week: a jit subcommand for Hazel's CLI, to prepare hybrid Hazel and JavaScript applications, like hazeljs-examples' (^ticket(899)).

Next week: a livelits PR, extending the livelits PR (^ticket(900)): for each hazeljs example, a node in a new tree of slides, Livelit applications, organized as the Hazel activities page is (ancient oracles, one-player games, Hazel AI opponents, physics simulation, automata).
